item.title: SAP source code incident, NFS2ROOT Linux flaw, Cacti zero-day
item.description:
SAP confirms a cybersecurity incident involving its GitHub source code, a twelve-year-old Linux NFS flaw called NFS2ROOT allows remote root access, and a Cacti zero-day has a public exploit. Also: pCloud Pass attack, a second exploited Drupal flaw, a Hex package manager warning and CERT-In's WhatsApp advisory.

Stories covered:

  • SAP confirms incident tied to GitHub source code — Sources: Techmeme, The Record, BleepingComputer, SecurityWeek
  • NFS2ROOT Linux flaw allows remote root access — Sources: BleepingComputer
  • Unpatched Cacti zero-day has public exploit — Sources: BleepingComputer
  • pCloud confirms attack on its password manager — Sources: BleepingComputer
  • Second Drupal takeover flaw exploited in attacks — Sources: BleepingComputer
  • Hex package manager warns of potential data breach — Sources: SecurityWeek
  • CERT-In flags five WhatsApp vulnerabilities — Sources: Inc42, MediaNama

item.description:

item.title: Palo Alto Fragnesia attacks, 1Password breach, VMware patches
item.description:
Attackers are exploiting the Fragnesia flaw against Palo Alto PAN-OS firewalls, 1Password disclosed a breach through an employee GitHub account, and VMware released its third critical advisory in a week. The episode also covers the Todoist breach, a fake job assessment campaign using malicious NuGet packages, ChatGPT's merged usage limits, and attacks on GeoServer.

  • VMware issues third critical advisory in a week — Sources: The Register Security

  • Fake job tests deliver malicious NuGet packages — Sources: Dark Reading
  • ChatGPT merges Chat and Work with one usage meter — Sources: TechCrunch
  • Two new GeoServer flaws under attack — Sources: SecurityWeek

item.title: Check Point servers hit, Radware key exposure, Microsoft Code Red
item.description:
Attackers compromised two dozen Check Point management servers, and Radware disclosed that customer cloud log export keys may have been exposed. Microsoft declared a Code Red after its November outage, and Google set new rules for AI agents in Workspace. The episode also covers the Inception extortion gang, a coding agent attack on a financial firm, and a Turnitin cyberattack.

Stories covered:

  • Google requires AI agents to use new Workspace gateways — Sources: The Next Web
  • New Inception extortion gang runs large vishing campaign — Sources: BleepingComputer
  • Turnitin discloses cyberattack on customer-facing systems — Sources: BleepingComputer

item.title: OpenRouter Drops 3 AI Hosts, GL.iNet Routers Hacked, Ghostscript Flaw
item.description:
Researchers found attackers copying prompts inside three AI inference providers, and OpenRouter removed them. GL.iNet confirmed hackers infected routers and KVM devices through its cloud, and a patched Ghostscript flaw lets crafted uploads run commands. The episode also covers Claude Code secret leaks, the Cleverbridge card breach, and Google's Agent Compute Engine.

  • Cleverbridge breach exposes card numbers and CVVs — Sources: BleepingComputer
  • Optimizely script attack hits 178 organizations — Sources: Help Net Security
  • Google announces Agent Compute Engine for AI agents — Sources: InfoQ

item.title: VMware vCenter zero-day, plus critical PHP and NGINX patches
item.description:
A China-linked group exploited a VMware vCenter flaw before Broadcom released a patch. PHP and F5 NGINX both shipped critical fixes, and ASUS patched its management console. The episode also covers vendor breaches at Chase, Visa and Mastercard, Meta's Muse agent, and Android developer verification.

  • ASUS fixes critical flaws in Control Center Express — Sources: BleepingComputer
  • Chase, Visa and Mastercard confirm vendor breaches — Sources: The Next Web, The Register Security, DataBreaches.net
  • Meta employees say AI agent Muse mixes up user data — Sources: TechCrunch
  • Android developer verification goes global in January 2027 — Sources: Help Net Security, Ars Technica

item.title: Java4Shell Java flaw, GPT-6.2 launch, Docker Hub key theft

A critical Java flaw called Java4Shell affects Jenkins, Jira and other major applications, and Oracle has patched it. OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, and researchers show cloud keys leaked in Docker Hub images are stolen within seconds. Also: the Microsoft 365 outage, a Fugaku supercomputer breach, a Gemini agent test and an FAA router pause.
